4. CONDITIONiNG 4.1 The test specimens shall be conditioned at 27 f 2�C and 65 & 5 percent relative humidity for not less than 16 hours. The test shall be carried out immediately after conditioning. 5. APPARATUS 5.1 Test Chamber and Cooling System - The test chamber shall consist of a well insulated box of approximate internal dimensions 400 x 1 000 x 150 mm, having viewing windows 900 f 10 mm apart. These windows shall be insulated with plugs of insulation between readings to ensure good temperature distribution. The chamber shall be fitted with a cooling system designed to give a low internal temperature distribution complying with the requirements of 7.
Now - A suitable chamber and cooling and illustrated in Fig. 1 and 2. Liquid nitrogen most satisfactory coolant. system is described in Appendix A has been found in practice to be the

5.2 Reference Length - Inside the box a reference length of 880 f 5 mm shall be positioned so that fiducial marks on the end are at the same level and in the same vertical plane as fiducial lines on the test specimen. The coefficient of expansion of the reference length material should be small and accurately known. A suitable material is silica in the form of a rod with ends ground to knife edges, as shown in Fig. 3. It shall be adequately supported to prevent bowing. 5.3 Measuring Systefn - A travelling microscope or equivalent capable of measuring to 0.01 mm shall be provided. Care shall be taken to ensure that the direction of travel of the instrument is parallel to the edge of` the test specimen; any divergence shall be less than one degree of arc. *Giossnry of trrms,
symbols and units rclnting to thermal insulation materials.

6. TEST SPECIMENS 6.1 The test specimen
dimensions: shall be a rectangular Length Width Thickness 900 f board 20 mm having the following

100 to 300 mm 25 to 50 mm

significant deformation of the original cell structure; the surfaces shall be parallel and unbowed and free of surface skins ( hot wire cutting is not permissible ). To each end of the board shall be fixed fiducial lines. These may consist of, for example, razor blades attached rigidly to the corners by drawing pins so that the knife edges project beyond the edge of the specimen and perpendicular to its length, as shown in Fig. 3.

length of both the test specimen with 11239 ( Part 1 )-1985". and the reference

7.2 Support the test specimen in the apparatus so that it does not sag and is free to move, and so that air may circulate freely round it. Position the end of the specimen carrying the fiducial lines centrally in the windows and symmetrically with respect to the reference length. 7.3 Insert the temperature measuring devices and switch on the fan ( if used ). After the temperature has been steady within f2"C for 30 minutes, measure the difference in length between the test specimen and the reference length. When the initial difference in length has been noted, adjust the thermostat to reduce the temperature by about 20�C and insert the plugs in the viewing holes. When the temperature is steady within 32�C for 20 minutes at the new level again measure the difference betweeen the length of the test specimen and the reference length. Repcat this measurement procedure at approximately 5 minutes intervals until three consecutive measurements agree to within O-03 mm. 7.4 Repeat the above procedure until the lowest temperature required is reached. Also make measurements as the apparatus is brought back to room temperature whilst observing the same precautions to establish thermal equilibrium. Check the temperature in the box before and after each measurement of length; the average of the total number of readings rhall he taken as the temperature to be associated with the length measured. The ditfcrence between the average temperature immediately before and after measurement shall not exceed 2�C and the corresponding differencc for any individual temperature measuring device shall not exceed 5�C. 8. CALCULATION

8.1 Use the results obtained to plot a graph of the length of the test specimen against temperature. Make allowance for the ( calculated ) change in the length of the reference length. Tile results should all lie on a smooth curve and there should be no significant hysteresis he tween descending and ascending temperature points. If there is significant hysteresis, repeat the determination allowing more time for the test specimen to attain thermal equilibrium.

APPENDIX
( Clause 5.1 )
SUITABLE A-l SUITABLE A-l.1 Test APPARATUS

A

APPARATUS

Chamber - A box ( see Fig. 1 ) made from a good low temperature insulating material. The internal dimensions of the box are approximately 400 x 1 000 x 150 mm with wall thickness of at least 100 mm. Zn the front of the box two tapered viewing holes of about 50 mm diameter and having centres 900 f 10 mm apart are cut so that the ends of the test specimen can be viewed under all temperature conditions. These holes are closed on the inside by thin glass sheet; plugs to fill the holes are provided. In the back of the box a cooling coil is fitted consisting of three turns of copper tubing of 5 mm nominal bore running the length of the box; the top limb is pierced with holes of l-5 mm diameter. The coil is closed at one end and the other end is connected to a liquid nitrogen container by a heavily insulated tube ( see Fig. 2 ) . A fan is installed in the box to minimize any temperature variation.
A-l.2 Cooling System - Liquid nitrogen is supplied to the cooling coil pressurizing the container with compressed air or nitrogen ( Fig. 2 ). The rate of flow of liquid nitrogen to the coil is regulated by a gas valve controlled by a thermostat which provides venting of the pressurizing air to atmosphere to reduce the pressure in the liquid nitrogen container and also to provide a vent for any boil-off from the liquid nitrogen container. A buffer vessel is provided in the compressed air system to eliminate `hunting' of the temperature control and a manometer with a range of about 20 kPa to indicate the air pressure to the required accuracy.
